                                              Message

       It is a great pleasure for me to be associated with Nehru College, Pailapool, the premier College
of Lakhipur Sub-Division of Cachar District.

        I delightfully welcome each and every student to this premier institute of learning. It is our vision
to provide the nation with motivated, responsible and disciplined youth to shape a better future.

         Education is the most powerful weapon which you can use to change the world. Our endeavour at
Nehru College is to equip the youth with relevant education which will help them not only to excel in
their field of study but also to contribute to the development of the country.

        Our experienced and dedicated faculty members ignite the young minds through strong
academics, co-curricular and extra-curricular activities which are aimed at total personality development
of the students. We equip them to take on challenges and develop in them a strong will power. We give
the students necessary support and encouragement they need to reach to their full potential.




                                    “WE MARCH ALONG WITH YOU

                                          FOR YOUR VICTORY’’




                                                                                                           4
                                        From the Principal ‘s Desk




Dear Parents, students and well-wishers of the Nehru College family, my prayerful greetings to all of you. It gives me
immense pleasure to welcome you and your child into the Nehru College family. First and foremost,I would like to express my
deep sentiments of gratitude to every one of you for your constant support, love and concern towards the College, which
enables and encourages us to strive hard to carry forward the mission of spreading value-based knowledge to one and all.

         Education is not an act of acquiring knowledge but learning a skill to lead life and forming one’s
personality. This is an ennobling process of growth. I can boldly say, that we have excelled in every initiative that
we undertook and we have stood together in facing the challenges in realizing quality education. We focus on
discovering, developing, drawing out the hidden talents and the magic lying dormant inside all of its students.
From academics to co-curricular activities, perseverance and a never-say-die spirit are entrenched in the heart of
every student, not only making them good students but brilliant beings. In today’s dynamic world, a 360-degree
development and grooming is of supreme importance and through our campus, we are creating an environment for
future leaders, entrepreneurs and professionals, who possess skills and aptitudes in an array of functional
disciplines.

        I am very happy, with the progress the College has made by imbibing in its students, value-based
education, synergized with modern teaching-learning methods, to produce a generation of well-informed and
emotionally-sound generation.

        We are partners in learning with our students and seek to deepen their knowledge, provide enriching and
innovative learning experiences, while also gently urging our students to come out of their comfort zone, to
attempt new challenges.

        I am positive that in times to come, we will continue this journey with elevated enthusiasm and persistently
provide a platform of holistic learning to the young generation of learners.

        Our students graduate with the skills, mind sets and qualities that will best equip them for success. Let’s
give our best and make this institution a modern temple of learning, through our diligence, devotion and
dedication.




                                                                                                                         5
 The College Profile


            Nehru College, nature’s rare and lovely darling, nestles down majestically among the
bounteous and ravishing ever-lush greenery besides the meandering sylvan Chiri like a shimmering
emerald concealed. A drive of just a kilometre’s journey from the burgeoning town, Pailapool, along the
Joypur-Harinagar Road, will take you definitely to this premier Institute of higher education at the tip of
the easternmost part of the Co-District of Lakhipur, Cachar.

            The College took its birth on the 28th of July, 1965 though the noble idea of establishing the
College was first mooted in a meeting held on the 8th of June, 1964, the day of Shraddha rituals of our
first ever Prime Minister, Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru. It was by way of commemorating as well as paying
homage to the great departed leader that the College was given the name after him.

             The College is located in an area which is basically predominated by socio-economically
backward classes as well as tea-garden workers. It was established in order to cater to the need of higher
education for the children of this locality and its neighbouring areas. The College aims more particularly
to uplift these sections of people of the society by spreading quality education amongst them.

The founder Principal of the College, Sri Khitish Chandra Das, M.A, (Double), B.T. was an eminent
educationist and being a man in humanitarian mould and a true Nehruvian in his persona, he came over to
this remote corner of far-flung countryside with the sole object of launching a crusade against the
encircling gloom of ignorance and illiteracy.

The College was fortunate enough to have the unflinching support of the local people and leaders, tea-
garden workers, business magnates and educated elites at the crucial moments of its nascent stage. In this
respect, the name of Sri Srinandan Dhubi deserves special mention. He donated 6 (six) Bighas of land
where the College is standing at present as a gift to the College when the affiliation of the College
assumed a big question. Within a short span of time, the College acquired more plots of land and now the
College has a vast expanded campus to facilitate the growing needs of the students.

              The College started its academic journey with very few students in 1965 in a small room at
the erstwhile Nehru High School, Pailapool. About one year later, it was shifted to its own building and
today, it is in full expedition with more than 1500 students on its rolls. It is not a miracle, nor a wonder at
all but a pointer to the fact that its entity and the key-role it plays in its domain are really beyond all
questions.

           At the time of inception, the College was affiliated to Gauhati University. But with the setting
up of Assam University, Silchar, today the Degree Course has come under the jurisdiction of Assam
University while the Secondary Course is under Assam State School Education Board (ASSEB, DIV-II)
Guwahati. Presently, the College comes under Government Provincialisation as per the Assam College
Employees Provincialisation Act, 2005.




                                                                                                             6
             The College is purely an Arts College. It offers Honours in some important subjects of Arts at
Bachelor Degree level, viz., English, Bengali, Manipuri, Hindi, Economics, Political Science and
History. Two new subjects: Education and Philosophy have been introduced since the academic session,
2013-2014. Sociology Department has also been opened from the Session 2024-25. The College has
introduced three new subjects for HS Course under NSQF/Skill subjects which are Fine Arts, IT/ITeS
and Office Management from academic session 2025-2026. This year, the College is introducing
Education, Logic & Philosophy and Sociology for HS Course. Feasibility of introducing Science and
Commerce streams is also being considered. Career-oriented courses like Computer Science, Remedial
Courses, etc. have already been started.

            The College is made up of five Blocks: viz. the Administrative Block, constructed under
RUSA 2.0, accommodates besides classrooms, Principal’s Room, Office Room, a Smart Classroom, a
well-equipped Fitness Gym, and a room for Games and Sports materials. Block A comprises of Faculty
Room, Examination Cell, Central Library, Classrooms (No. 1-10), Computer Centre, Language Lab and a
Canteen. Block B houses three huge Halls besides a number of mid-sized classrooms. Block C houses
separate rooms for NCC boys, NCC girls, NSS, RUSA, IQAC, Education Practical Lab, Health Centre,
Girls’ Common Room and KKHSOU Study Centre. Block D comprises of Seminar & Conference Room
as well as a Museum. The college has a huge Auditorium too. It also has a separate Boys’ Common
Room.The College Central Library is semi-digitalised which consists of a huge building having more
than twenty thousand (20,000) books in its stock along with a spacious Reading Room, a resourceful
reference section, with print and online journals, among others.

            Besides, the College has a newly constructed Girls’ Hostel too under UGC fund. Some more
Seminar / Conference Halls are in the offing. The College is indeed expanding its infra-structures with
the financial aids received from the Government, UGC and RUSA 2.0

            The College is proud of its Museum, the first of its kind amongst the Colleges in the Barak
Valley. It has enabled the College to preserve antiquities, natural objects and ethnic artefacts of rare
importance. It is heartening to note that a group of members of Jadavpur University, Kolkata came to
visit the Museum and study the materials and objects preserved in it. The group appreciated some of the
terracotta objects of the Museum.

            The College was first inspected by the NAAC Peer Team in September 2004 and accreditated
with ‘C ’ grade. It was again re-assessed by the NAAC Peer Team in September 2015. Recently, in the
       ++

month of January, 2025, the college has gone through its third phase of NAAC Peer Team Visit and has
been re-accreditated with ‘B’ grade.

            The College had celebrated its Golden Jubilee from 21st to 23rd September,2015. It is a
milestone in the history of the College thereby proving its relentless service to the young citizens which
is indeed a realization of the noble objectives cherished by its founding fathers and all those who are the
basic sustaining force behind the College.

            Indeed, the College has come a long way as symbol of aspirations of the public in general for
higher education. Still there are miles to go for the College to achieve its full stature of growth and
prosperity and for this, the College authority is looking forward to the spontaneous support and never-
failing co-operation from all sections of people in the days to come.

 Mission & Vision
      Propagation, Cultivation and Spreading of Knowledge from one generation to another for the
      enrichment of the society in particular and the nation at large, to realise the ideals of
      “HUMANITY”, “TOLERANCE” AND “MAGNANIMITY” cherished by our beloved
      Prime Minister Late Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru.




Goal
Advancement of Higher Education by imparting quality education for the uplift of all the
sections of the society.



Objectives
To encourage diverse sections of the society to strive for the optimum development of their innate potential.
Toenable such sections to become fully aware of their human rights and responsibilities and inspire them to
enjoy these rights by sincerely exercising their responsibilities.

To inculcate scientific temper to re-orient societal attitudes and prejudices with profound sense of patriotism.
To establish contacts or build partnership with different societal groups, institutional as well as business
organisations for realisation of such diverse objectives as in the fields of health care, career guidance, employment
opportunities and other related areas.

 COURSES OF STUDIES
TWO YEAR HIGHER SECONDARY (H.S) COURSE IN ARTS

1. Two-Year Higher Secondary Course is governed by the Rules and Regulations of Assam State School Education
Board, Div-II, Guwahati. It contains two Examination: (i) First Year and (ii) Secondary Year.
2. Subjects, combination and course-structure of two-year Higher Secondary Course in Arts (as per facilities
available in the college)
         Part-A:Core Subjects              : (1)English
                                               (2) Any one: M.I.L. Manipuri/Bengali/Hindi/Hmaror Alternative
                                               English.
                                               (3) Environmental Education
         Part-B:Elective Subjects              : Any three: Political Science, Economics, History, Education, Logic &
                                               Philosophy and Sociology.
         Part-C:NSQF/Skill Subjects            : Any one: Advance Bengali, Advance Manipuri, AdvanceHindi,
                                               Advance Assamese, Fine Arts, IT/ITeS and Office Management.


                  A student can select any one of the language papers listed in No. 2 of Part-A as his/her M.I.L.
         subject. The College has all these language papers taught in their respective departments. If any student
         wishes to opt for language paper e.g. Assamese, other than any of the above language papers, he/she can
         do that on his/her own with special permission from the Board.
3. Year wise course structure and distribution of marks for Higher Secondary Course in Arts shall be as
follows:
                    Subjects                                       1st Year                       2nd Year
Core                (i)        English                 Marks     100                    Marks      100
                                                       (one paper only)                 (one paper only)
                    (ii)       MIL/Alternative         Marks     100                    Marks     100
                               English
                                                       (one paper only)                 (one paper only)
Elective                  Any three Subjects           Marks     300                    Marks     300
                                                       (100 marks per subject)          (100 marks per subject)
Total                        5 subjects                          500 marks                       500 marks


4. H.S. First Year Examination:
  i.       HS First Year Examination will be held at the end of First Year class. It will be conducted by the Board
           at the centre of examination in March every year.

  ii.      Each subject carries a total of 100 marks.

  iii.     First Year marks will not be included in Second Year. They are meant for only promotion to Second
           Year

  iv.      A student may choose one additional/optional subject from among the NSQF/Skill subjects.
                                                                                                                  10
      v.          Additional/optional subject carries no extra benefits of marks but will be considered as an Elective
                 Subject in case the student fails in any of the Elective subjects.

     vi.         In the course curricula of ASSEB, DIV-II, the subject Environment Education is compulsory for the
                 students of all the streams in HS First Year Course. The student will be assessed through written
                 examination and project work. Though total marks of 50 are allotted for the subject but the obtained
                 marks are not calculated in the overall result. Instead, grade is awarded on the basis of the marks
                 obtained by the learner.


                 The Grading Scheme for the subject is as follows:

                  Grade                                                  Percentage                                          Marking range
                   A ...................................................... 80%---100% .......................................    40-50
                   B..........................................................60%---79% .......................................   30-39
                   C..........................................................40%---59% ........................................ 20-29
                   D......................................................... 0%---39%   ........................................ 0-19

     vii.        The result of the First Year Examination will be declared on the basis of the criteria fixed by the
                 ASSEB, DIV-II.

5.            HS Final Examination:

      (i)         HS Final Examination will be held at the end of Second Year. It will be conducted by the Board at the
                  Centre of Examination in February / March every year.
      (ii)        Each subject carries 100 marks.
      (iii)       The results of the HS Final Examination will be determined on the basis of marks obtained in HS Final
                  Examination only. (Performance of a student in the HS First Year Examination will not be taken into
                  account while declaring the performance of the student in the Final Examination).

6.            Pass Marks

      (a) A student shall be declared pass only when he/she secures the minimum marks prescribed in each of the
              two core and three elective subjects. The pass marks will be 33% of the total marks for all subjects. In the
              case of candidate offering four elective subjects, the marks secured in three subjects, where the candidate’s
              performance is better will be taken into account for determining pass, rank, division, distinction and star
              marks. The marks secured in the fourth elective subject (with poorest performance) will however, be
              shown in the marks-sheet. The marks secured in the fourth elective subject will not be taken into account
              for awarding rank, division, distinction and star. Conditions for award of division, distinction and star are
              given here under in clause (b), (c) and (d).

      (b) A successful candidate obtaining 60% and above marks in aggregate will be placed in First Division.
              Those obtaining 45% and above but less than 60% marks in aggregate will be placed in Second Division.
              Other successful candidates obtaining less than 45% marks in aggregate will be placed in Third Division.



      (c) If a successful candidate obtains 80% or more marks, he/she will be declared to have secured
              ‘DISTINCTION’ in that subject.

      (d) A candidate obtaining 75% or more above of the total allotted marks (in two core and three elective
              subjects) will be declared to have secured ‘STAR MARKS’.

 RULES & REGULATIONS
UNFAIR MEANS IN EXAMINATIONS:

Rules / Regulations:To curb unfairmeans in the HS Examinations, Rules and Regulations of ASSEB, DIV-II,
Guwahati shall be strictly followed.

CLASS ATTENDANCE:

i)Each student shall have to attend a minimum of 75% Lectures/Tutorials/Practical classes in each subject of both
the courses as per the recommended Course Structure of the concerned programme of study.

ii) Class Attendance shall be calculated based on actual number of classes held during each year in eachsubject.
Number of decimal be rounded off to next higher number (e.g. 74.01% be rounded off to 75%).

iii) Only the students with 75% and above of attendance in allsubjectsshall be allowed to appear in the Final
Examinations.

iv) Period/ days during which students attend to represent the Nation/ State/ University/College in
differentRegional, National and International Events of Sports/ Cultural/ NCC/ NSS etc. may be treated as class
attendance for the actual number of days, subject to a maximum of 20 (twenty) days.

v) There is a provision of condonation of attendance to be accorded by the Principal of the college for thestudents
who have secured the attendance between 64% and 74%, purely on medical grounds and onproduction of Medical
Certificate from the Competent Authority. Prayer for such condonation shall berouted through the Head of the
Department.




(A)ADMISSION PROCEDURE AND CRITERIA

The exact number of seats in Higher Secondary FirstYear is fixedas per the instruction of Assam State School
Education Board, DIV-II.

 For admission to Higher Secondary First Year classes, candidates who have passed HSLC under
SEBA,Assam/ ASSEB, DIV-I, shall be considered eligible. In case of candidates hailing from other States or
Board (s) but having high academic record, this criterion can be relaxed with the submission of Migration
Certificate.

Admission to the college is purely online. Candidates opting for admission to the college should apply / register
on the Darpan Portal byvisiting the site, www.darpan.ahseconline.in or www.ahsec.assam.govt.inmentioning /
selecting the College name in the prescribed application form.

While filling up the Admission form, an applicant should pay attention to the matter of choosing the right
combination of his/her interest. Any change in the combination should be made within 30days from the date of
commencement of classes subject to information and approval of the Principal.

Admission process shall be solely reserved by the Admission Committee constituted for the purpose.


                                                                                                                12
 Notices containing the norms, date of interview, admission etc. shall be pasted up in the College Notice Board
and the College Website generally within a week from the date of publication of the Results of the qualifying
Examinations.

Admission shall be made strictly in order of merit as per College Admission Rule framed by the Admission
Committee. The Committee’s decision regarding admission shall stand final.

Any pressure / interference of any sort in the matter(s) of admission shall be treated as disqualification
amounting to forfeiture of claim for admission.

Attested copies of the following documents must be furnished along with the application form for the
admission:

    1. Mark-sheets, Certificate of H.S.L.C. and other qualifying Examinations.
    2. S.C./S.T./O.B.C./ Certificate.
    3. Gap-certificate in case of student passed earlier than the current year.
    4. Migration Certificate in case of students from other State(s) / Board(s).
    5. Three copies of latest passport size photographs for (i) Identity Card cum Fee Card. (ii) Admission form
        and (iii) Library Card.
    6. Candidates shall produce the original copies of the certificates mentioned above at the time of interview.
    7. A photo of the candidate planting a sapling should also be included with the Admission form.(In case of
        BPL candidates)

(c) ADMISSION OF UNSUCCESSFUL CANDIDATES
Unsuccessful candidates in H.S First/Second Year shall appear at the subsequent Final Examination of the Board
as non-collegiate candidates.

The fee structure for admission to H.S First/Second Year for the Session 2026-2027 will be as per latest Govt.

     b) Undertaking from the students for fee studentship of HS-I& II that neither his nor her parents are

Examinations and Attendance Rules for H.S. Students:

1.Students must appear in all the assessment examinations of the College such as Test/Terminal Examinations and Class
Examinations held in a year. Sending up to the Final Examination is subject to the performance of the students in these
examinations. In the case of absentees, the college authorities will take decisions as per regulations.



2. A student must attend a minimum of 75% of the lectures delivered in each subject to be eligible to appear at the Board
Examination as a Collegiate/Regular student and minimum of 60% of the lectures delivered in each subject to be eligible to
appear in the Board Examination as a Non-Collegiate candidate. Any student with attendance below 60% will be considered
asDis-Collegiateand will not be eligible for appearing in the Board Examination.

 Literary and Research Oriented Activities
“The College Magazine is known as NEHRU COLLEGE STUDENTS’ MAGAZINE”. It is published annually as an
incorporation of four major languages.

    (i)      English            (ii) Bengali    (iii) Manipuri and        (iv) Hindi .

There is also aMulti-lingual wall magazine in the name of ‘KASTURI’.

Besides the College has a research-oriented magazine with ISBN No. under the name and style “THE NEW HORIZON”
published annually by the Research & Publication Cell.

Academic Activities
The College organises departmental seminars, workshops, field activities, UGC sponsored National Seminars along with
excursions almost every year for the benefit of the teachers, students and the local people at large. It also conducts UGC
sponsored Certificate Courses on Functional English. Besides, the college has opened a study centre of KKHSOU, Guwahati
for U.G & PG Students since 2016.




                                                 Facilities Available
Library
    The College library consists of a digital Central Library, Departmental library and a Book Bank. The Departmental library
has a good stock of books for the teachers and students of different departments while the Book Bank has a considerable
number of books of different genres for the students. The Central library which is the indispensable part of the College library
is well equipped with a vast treasure of books. It has more than 21,000 books and subscribes to selected newspapers,
journals/E-journals/E-books and periodicals. These are kept well displayed in the specific racks of the Reading Room which is
spacious enough to accommodate a good number of readers. Adjacent to Reading Room is the lending section to facilitate
lending and borrowing transactions. Over and above, the college distributes free textbooks to the students that are sent by the
Council through the library, the information of which shall be notified by the latter.

             Students are provided with Reader’s Tickets and Borrower’s Card.Reader’s Ticket meant for the Reading Room
while Borrower’s Card enables them to take out one book on loan for 07 days from the date of issue subject to renewal. These
cards arenon-transferable and must be returned at the end of the session. Fine of ₹1/- per day will be imposed if books are not
returned in due time. In case of loss, damage or mutilation of borrowed books the borrower shall be liable to replace it at
his/her own cost or to pay fine.

Library Opening Hours:                 Week days: 10:30 AM to 4:00 PM.

Return of Books             :                  11:00 AM to1:30 PM

Issue of Books             :                       2:00 PM to 4:00 PM.

Sports & Gym:
          College has a well-equipped Gym room constructed under RUSA 2.0. Also the College has a variety of Sports
Facilities purchased under RUSA 2.0 along with a Basket Ball Court.




                                                                                                                             15
 Language Lab:
         To enable the students to have proficiency over different languages, the College has a well-equipped language
laboratory. It aims to help the students to hear the language spoken from recorded tapes and to practice speaking in the same
manner.

Computer Lab:
         The College has a well-equipped computer lab to enable the development of digital skill amongst the students.

Common Room:
    There are two separate Common Rooms for boys and girls. During off-periods, boy and girl students have to stay in their
respective common rooms. For better utilization of their leisure time, facilities of indoor games are provided in these common
rooms.

Canteen:
There is also a well-equipped CANTEEN for refreshment of students and staffin the College campus.

Museum:
The College is proud of its museum, the first of its kind amongst the Colleges of Barak Valley. It has enabled the College to
preserve antiquities, natural objects and ethnic artefacts of rare importance.



Cultural Activities
 (i)   In keeping with the custom of the College, Freshers’ Welcome Ceremony will be organised by the Students’Union.
 (ii)  Annual College festival will be held in the college campus by the second week of January at the latest. Social festivals
       such as Saraswati Puja, Martyrs’ Day, Sarad Utsav, Hindi Divas, and so on, etc. will be held according to calendar
       dates/convenience.
 (iii) The Foundation Day of the College which falls on 1st of July is also observed from the year 2023 in a befitting manner.


Scholarship
1. Students are entitled to apply for SC/ST/OBC/MOBC and merit scholarship that may be notified from time to time.

2. The College has a fund known as “Student Aid Fund”. It has been constituted to provide financial help to the students
belonging to the economically weaker section of the society. The committee of the fund determines the quantum of aid to the
suitable candidates. Further information regarding the matter be collected from the office.

3. Students who have secured good results in H.S. are usually felicitated on special occasions.


Students Travel Concession
  Students are entitled to enjoy Travelling concession. Details relating to the matter can be obtained from the office of the
College.


NCC, NSS, etc.
The College provides facilities for N.C.C. for boys’wing under 3rd Assam Battalion and for girls’ wing under 62 Assam
Battalion. The College has also an NSS unit sponsored by the Ministry of HRD.

Students’ Union

The College has a Students’ Union known as Nehru College Students’ Union. It is headed by the Principal as ex-officio
President. All the office-bearers of the Union are elected through secret ballots from amongst the students themselves. Election
to the office of the Union is generally held as per the scheduled date.The tenure of office of the Union is only one year.

 General Rules for Maintenance of Discipline
i) The College is greatly concerned with the education of the students. It lays great emphasis on discipline and character-
     building and as such students studying in the College are obliged to maintain a high standard of discipline. They are
     subjected to the rules and regulations as prescribed by the College authorities. Violation of these rules, irregularity in
     attendance, irregularity in clearance of college fees, adoption of unfair means during examinations,unsatisfactory
     progress, showing discourtesy to the teachers are liable to disciplinary actions like termination of scholarship, forfeiture of
     the College certificates, forced transfer and even rustication / expulsion from the college.
ii) While in the campus of the College or outside, student must always carry their photo-identity cards issued to them by the
     College authority. They are required to produce the photo-identity cards on demand, failing which they may be debarred
     from attending classes/college.
iii) Students’ Union shall be subjected to such rules and regulations that the College administration may describe from time to
     time.
iv) Any notice of the Union, if to be pasted/circulated anywhere in the College by the students, shall require prior approval of
     the College authority.
v) All powers relating to discipline and disciplinary action in relation to the students of the College shall vest in the Principal
     of the College and his decision/verdict be final in all such matters.

    Health & Hygiene Cell, an Extension Service Cell, a Women’s Cell, etc.
